newsitem.title: ITALY: KPMG opens office in Albania, its 147th country.
newsitem.headline: KPMG opens office in Albania, its 147th country.

text.p: Accounting and consultancy company KPMG said it has opened an office in Albania, the 147th country in the world where the firm now operates.
The international auditing company said in a statement the head of the new office in Tirana was Orazio Vagnozzi, an Italian who was formerly a senior manager in Los Angeles and Milan.
KPMG, which has just opened an office in Moldavia, said Albania was currently the East European country with the highest rate of economic growth and social reforms.
It was aiming for a client base formed mainly by international companies already present in Albania, local companies about to be privatised and foreign investors interested in the nation's potential.
KPMG, with 819 offices in 147 countries, said it posted global turnover for the year to end-September 1996 of $8.1 billion, a rise of eight percent on the previous year.
In Italy, where KPMG SpA has been operating for 40 years, the company has 22 offices and had turnover of 110 billion lire ($73 million) for the year to end-September.
